records.text: The Defilers Emissary invites visitors to join the battle, serving as a battleground recruiter for the Defilers. The emissary can turn away those deemed not yet powerful enough.

The League of Arathor Emissary urges visitors not to neglect Azeroth while exploring new lands, calling for help against the Defilers so their resources can be secured. The emissary offers a chance to join the battle.

The Silverwing Emissary recruits for Warsong Gulch and frankly admits the Silverwing side needs help against its opponents. The emissary appeals to the honor of joining the fight and says the Silverwing Sentinels will look more favorably on those who help.

The Stormpike Emissary seeks aid for the Stormpike Guard against the Frostwolf Clan in Alterac Valley, presenting the battle as an opportunity for honor and repute. Visitors can choose to join the battle.

The Warsong Emissary represents the Warsong Outriders in the call to fight in Warsong Gulch against the Silverwing Sentinels. Its greeting presents the battle as a chance to earn honor and reputation, and it offers an option to join.

The Frostwolf Emissary calls for help in Alterac Valley and sets a strength threshold for joining the fight. Its greeting makes clear that an aspiring combatant must first become stronger; the emissary’s name identifies its Frostwolf affiliation.

The Lunar Festival Harbinger travels from Moonglade to bring the festival to far-flung communities, welcoming visitors to join its celebration. After a visitor completes the fireworks display, the harbinger offers an invitation to Moonglade; it can also provide a replacement invitation through its greeting.

Lady Liadrin, Blood Knight Matriarch, evaluates the orphan Salandria’s unusual gift for channeling power from M’uru. Seeing promise in the child, she says she will petition for Salandria’s custody and proper Blood Knight training in Silvermoon, and asks the escort to keep her safe until then.

Khadgar of the Sons of Lothar discusses strategy with A'dal in Shattrath and arranges for a summoned servant to orient newcomers. He reveres the naaru's wisdom, says A'dal has taught him more than years in Dalaran's libraries, and credits A'dal's will with protecting the city. After becoming stranded in Outland, he split and hid the key to Karazhan; he seeks its fragments as formerly safe hiding places become dangerous.

A'dal is a naaru in Shattrath who communicates through light, melodic chimes and thoughts, offering visitors an assurance of safety. A'dal supports the Sha'tar's struggle to reclaim Tempest Keep and tests would-be allies through trials of mercy and tenacity. Saving prisoners threatened by Kargath Bladefist and protecting the stranded Millhouse Manastorm embody those standards.

Wind Trader Lathrai deals in exotic engineering goods gathered from far away and attracts customers to the World's End Tavern because of what he sells. After Skithian arakkoa steal a large shipment of his goods, he sets about recovering it and questions visitors about a Broken merchant connected to his trade.
G'eras offers goods to visitors who ask to browse his wares in Shattrath City.

Voren'thal is a seer among the Scryers who seeks to expose Kael'thas's allegiance to new masters. He studies how to condense the power of arcane tomes into runes. Frail health prevents him from joining the fight against Socrethar in person, so he offers an object through which he can project his power across Outland.

Magistrix Fyalenn is a Scryer who left Kael'thas's following and considers that choice the best any of them made. She believes his followers are blind or afraid of where he is leading them, and speaks as one of the people now opposing his forces. The Scryers' conflict with Kael's armies is personal as well as military: she asks supporters to contribute to the fight and insists that even small efforts count.

Adyen is an Aldor Lightwarden whose duties are to protect the priesthood and destroy the Light's enemies. He opposes the Burning Legion and its allies, while holding to the naaru's law that a lost brother should be offered a chance to repent before destruction. At Socrethar's confrontation, Adyen appeals to Kaylaan as a former pupil whose will he remembers from childhood, then stands by his companions' faith and prepares to fight Socrethar.

Ishanah is the Aldor's High Priestess, welcoming outsiders as a servant of the Sha'tar and safeguarding sacred sites through the Light. Against Socrethar, she favors strong-willed companions over armies vulnerable to corruption. She offers herself as a prisoner to free Kaylaan. If Kaylaan is lost in battle, she grieves that even her strongest prayer could not raise him, finding solace in his final resistance to corruption. She remembers Socrethar as a renowned warrior of the Light whose flaw was pride.
An arcanist of the Scryers.
An Aldor vindicator serving the Sha'tar who welcomes visitors to Aldor Rise and offers guidance to places such as the bank and the World's End Tavern.
The Scryer Arcane Guardian serves as a guide in Shattrath, offering directions to the World's End Tavern and the bank.

Sal'salabim is a mo'arg in Shattrath's Lower City who drinks at the bar and deals in debts. He makes help for Altruis conditional on collecting gold owed by Raliq, Coosh'coosh, and Floon, then gives Altruis information about turning fel cannons against structures. He points out that overseers hold the keys needed for the plan. His dealings with Altruis mix practical assistance with self-interest.
Raliq the Drunk is one of Sal'salabim's named debtors. When confronted with Sal'salabim's demand for payment, he answers with a threat to teach the collector a lesson.
A Scryer retainer found in Netherstorm and Shattrath City.

On Scryer's Tier in Shattrath, Dathris Sunstriker directs able people to report to Larethor at the Sunwell Plateau. The mission requires the Scryers and Aldor to set aside their differences; Dathris says he has little more information and warns that the situation sounds serious.

Arcanist Adyria, of the Scryers, procures basilisk eyes for the elixir meant to sharpen Voren'thal's prophetic visions. She explains that his visions warned of Kael'thas's destructive path and that his usual ethereal supplier has failed her. She asks for more eyes because the visions may affect her people's fate.

Sha'nir is an Aldor healer caring for Shattrath's growing number of refugees. With antidotes running low, she seeks dreadfang venom sacs to treat their poison wounds. She also pursues a traditional cure for Zahlia, who lost her sight after a head injury: blood from the long-lived basilisk Stonegazer, so Zahlia may see her son again.
An injured refugee in Shattrath, identified by displacement and injury rather than by a personal name.
Iz'zard is a humanoid found in Shattrath City.
Zahlia is a woman who survived a severe head injury and lost her eyesight. Sha'nir describes Stonegazer, an old basilisk, as the source of blood sought for a traditional cure.

Seth is a child from Lakeshire who misses fishing with his friends. His mother has stopped him visiting a nearby lake because of its dangers, though he dismisses the spiders there as harmless. He also compares the Aldor's rebuilding work in Shattrath with a foreman and bridge repairs back home.
Haris Pilton is a Shattrath socialite who sells goods. Their brief remarks use slang, call things “hot,” and brush things off with “whatever.”
Tinkerbell is Haris Pilton's pet and an animal.

Mehlisah Highcrown represents the Lower City and coordinates its response to the Shadow Council at Auchindoun. She relies on spies there and sends field commander Mahfuun to brief people at the Shadow Labyrinth; she also expects To’gun and Grik’tha to assist one another. After Murmur is defeated, she reflects on how close it came to escaping and credits the effort to contain the Shadow Council threat. She is practical and protective of Outland’s peoples, whose suffering she says has already been too great.

Nutral is a flight master who arranges travel by air. He understands that some travelers would rather learn to fly their own mounts than be carried between destinations, even though that could cost him business, and points them toward flight instructors in Shadowmoon Valley. His advice is friendly and pragmatic.

Nicole Bartlett is the matron of an orphanage for children of Outland who have lost their parents and lack someone to care for them. She welcomes visitors and asks whether they are considering adoption.
Mendorn is a banker who offers customers access to banking services.
Ahemen is a staff vendor who lets customers browse his goods.
Oloraak is a fish merchant who pitches fresh fish, calling it the freshest and inviting customers to sample his wares.
Minalei invites visitors to sit and make themselves comfortable, and offers the service of making the inn their home.
Lissaf sells blades and boasts of their quality, claiming their workmanship and care are unmatched while urging customers to buy.
Karokka is a poison-supplies vendor who offers goods for customers to browse.
Garul is a food and drink vendor. Visitors can browse his goods.
Araac bluntly asks what the visitor is staring at.

Lorokeem is an arakkoa alchemist whose specialty is elixirs. He is pursuing an elixir of eternal life and believes rare essences from the Caverns of Time could help his research. He welcomes students who demonstrate skill and is willing to teach his craft.
Hamanar teaches jewelcrafting.
Leatei is a humanoid.
Inessera sells jewelcrafting supplies.
Skreah is a vendor of alchemy supplies, ready to show customers the goods on offer.
Skettis Outcast is a humanoid that performs an emote while out of combat.
A High Elf refugee found in Shattrath City.
A Dwarf refugee.
A Broken refugee.
The Anchorite Attendant offers a quiet assent: “May it be so.”
An Aldor anchorite found among the settlements of the western Outland frontier.
A Mag'har refugee in the western Outland settlements, identified as one of the displaced orcish people rather than as a named individual. Its idle behavior includes an emote.
An Aldor neophyte in the settlements of the western Outland frontier, a novice associated with the Aldor.
A sporeling refugee in the western Outland settlements, identified as a displaced member of the sporeling people.
An Aldor neophyte serving as a combatant in the western Outland settlements.
A Lost One refugee in the western Outland settlements, identified as a displaced member of the Lost Ones.
A refugee child found in Shattrath City.
A child among the refugees found in the region.
A peasant refugee among those gathered in the region.
Seymour is a master skinning trainer who frames instruction around whether visitors have honed their skills.
Shaarubo tends the bar and offers goods to browse.
Mildred Fletcher is a physician and First Aid trainer. She points learners toward Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen in Theramore for further training.

Jack Trapper is a cook and trainer who frames his work with a fishing proverb: people may learn to fish, he says, but the fish may need cooking, which is where he comes in. His joke ties his training role to a cook’s practical craft.
Kylene is a barmaid who serves drinks and is also associated with cooking. She greets customers with the familiar “What’ll it be, sweety?”
As a master leatherworking trainer, Darmari asks whether a learner has honed their skills enough for his teaching.
Ernie Packwell is a trade-goods vendor whose counter offers customers goods to browse. His title presents a general trade-goods role.
Jim Saltit sells cooking supplies, giving his vendor role a clear culinary focus.

Cro Threadstrong sells leatherworking supplies while caught in a tense dispute with a fruit seller whose cart obstructs the area. He warns the seller to move it and says that, with war approaching and an ogre enlisted on the other side, he will have to recruit help too. His words make him sound wary and ready to answer the threat.
Eral is a general-goods merchant in Shattrath, offering visitors a broad range of everyday goods.

Emissary Mordin receives Nether Residue in Shattrath for the Shattered Sun Offensive's war effort. The residue helps make oils that strengthen troops' weapons and armor against Kil'jaeden's allies; Outland's herbs, ores, and beasts can bear it.
Eiin sells specialty tailoring supplies in Shattrath, serving visitors who need materials for the tailoring trade.

Grand Anchorite Almonen welcomes visitors to the temple and sees it as his calling to share revealed truths. He credits A'dal with generous revelations, urging his listeners to embrace the Light and reject darkness as the forces of darkness threaten them.
Granny Smith is a fruit seller in Shattrath. She frets over missing apples, then hears an orc yelling and hopes someone will check on him, showing concern beyond her stall.

Griftah, who calls himself “Amazing Amulets,” is a flamboyant peddler whose patter turns every worry into a sale: a tikbalang ward, a love medallion, protection from death, or dungeon loot. He jokes at customers’ expense while insisting his charms work, and claims jewelcrafters cannot match his old mystical methods. He sends adventurers to his old friend Budd for a project; when presented with a voodoo doll, he recognizes its supposed mojo and parts with a small charm.

Innkeeper Haelthol offers shelter in the shattered lands, describing his help modestly as “what shelter I can.” His innkeeper role centers on lodging and goods for visitors, giving his greeting a practical, hospitable tone.
Yurial Soulwater sells enchanting supplies in Shattrath, serving visitors who come to browse his goods.
Amshesha Stilldark sells reagents from her stall in Shattrath’s Lower City, serving visitors who come to browse her goods.
Quelama Lightblade serves as a wand vendor in the settlement. Visitors can browse her goods, and she also offers repairs.
Urumir Stavebright serves as a staff vendor in the settlement. Visitors can browse his goods, and he also offers repairs.
Mahir Redstroke sells daggers and poison as a vendor in the settlement, and also offers repairs.
Selanam the Blade sells swords in the settlement and offers repairs.
Olodam Farhollow is a humanoid in Shattrath City.
Nalama the Merchant sells general goods in the settlement.
Trader Endernor is a trade-goods vendor; customers can browse his goods.
Vinemaster Alamaro is a wine vendor, distinguished by the goods he sells.
Berudan Keysworn is a banker who lets customers access their bank.
Enchanter Salias is identified as an apprentice enchanter.
Enchantress Metura is identified as an apprentice enchanter.
Enchanter Aeldron is identified as an apprentice enchanter.
Enchantress Volali is an enchanting trainer in Shattrath. She offers training.

High Enchanter Bardolan is Shattrath’s master enchanting trainer. His greeting asks visitors whether they have honed their skills enough to learn what he teaches, presenting his instruction as a step beyond basic training.

Shattrath Saul works the crowd with announcements for Perry Gatner’s comedy and the Tauren Chieftains’ live show at the World’s End Tavern, repeating the venue and show time to draw an audience. In his rock-show pitch, he even urges the banished to sneak back into Shattrath, giving his promotion a cheeky, high-energy edge.

Albert Quarksprocket hosts Shattrath entertainment, welcoming the audience and introducing Perry Gatner as the city’s best. After the act, he announces that the cantina is open all night and invites the crowd to stay and enjoy themselves.
The Vagrant is a Shattrath beggar who repeatedly asks passersby for spare copper. He pleads not to be ignored and says he has five children to feed, making his appeal personal and urgent.
Gromden is a banker, identified by that title and the bank service offered to visitors.
Quartermaster Endarin serves as an Aldor quartermaster. His title identifies the group he represents, and his shop offers goods to visitors.
Lisrythe Bloodwatch is known as the Fence, a vendor whose shop offers goods to visitors.
Quartermaster Enuril serves as a Scryer quartermaster. His title identifies the group he represents, and his shop offers goods to visitors.
An Aldor marksman in Shattrath City.
L'lura Goldspun is a banker in Shattrath.
Mi'irku Farstep serves as a portal trainer. He tells prospective learners that only mages can learn portal magic and asks whether a mage has come to learn it.

Harbinger Erothem addresses Anchorite Nindumen by name and asks him to pray for another inexperienced squad sent into Nagrand. He frames the request around the squad's deployment and answers, “May it be so.”
Neophyte Nemarn is a humanoid in Shattrath City.

Anchorite Nindumen responds warmly to Erothem and considers praying for the inexperienced squad sent into Nagrand an honor. His words ask the Light to aid their struggle, bless their ancient home, and grant tolerance for its elven visitors.
A mounted neophyte in Shattrath City.

Harbinger Haronem investigates reports of dark distortions around Oshu'gun as part of the Sunwell campaign, despite dismissing the inventor behind the multiphase goggles as a crackpot. He needs readings from the Spirit Fields and complains about Doctor Wafflefry's interruptions and inventions, while still pressing on with the investigation.

Magister Falris is a Shattrath magister with a sharp, partisan resentment of the Aldor's favor with the Sha'tar and their display of devotion near A'dal. He regards Haronem's regiment, known for cooking together rather than taking long lunch breaks, as a target for retribution, and imagines a prank on their meal as comic.
Viggz Shinesparked is Shattrath's engineering-supplies vendor.
Aaron Hollman supplies blacksmithing goods in Shattrath and also offers equipment repair.
Madame Ruby is Shattrath's enchanting-supplies vendor.

Muffin Man Moser is a bread merchant whose wares and self-description center on muffins. He cheerfully advertises them, jokes that he is called the muffin man because he sells muffins, and pairs his “magnificent muffins” with a tankard.
Ewe is a low-level animal in the Shattrath area, represented as a critter.
Fantei is a reagent vendor in Shattrath. The greeting associated with Fantei advertises a fine selection of reagents, presenting the shop as a useful stop for visitors seeking them.

A war veteran welcoming newcomers to Shattrath, this Haggard veteran describes the city as a rare place of safety in Outland. He recommends meeting A'dal, leader of the Sha'tar, inside the Terrace of Light and regards the naaru as an awe-inspiring sight.
Shattrath's peacekeepers help visitors find their way around the city. This peacekeeper welcomes people and offers guidance, with directions pointing to the World's End Tavern and the bank.
A demon associated with the Scryer Vault in Shattrath.
An Aldor acolyte in Shattrath, this humanoid represents the Aldor order.

Ezekiel is a Shattrath figure caught up in a search for the Book of the Dead. He first denies knowing it, then admits he lied: the book was stolen, probably by refugees, and he directs the search toward the ruffians. He says Auchindoun no longer needs it.
Ricole Nichie is identified as an ex-socialite in Shattrath.

“Dirty” Larry is a ruffian who threatens visitors and warns them to leave before he sets his dogs on them. When pressed about the Book of the Dead, he admits that his group had it and sold it to draenei for gold; the buyer spoke of a “master’s grand design.”
“Epic” Malone is a named ruffian in Shattrath.
“Creepjack” is a named ruffian in Shattrath.

Goblin Commoner is a recurring seasonal speaker. During the Lunar Festival, this goblin urges people to seek their elders’ wisdom and recounts the legend of Omen in Lake Elune’ara; other lines celebrate fireworks and the holidays.
Farmer Griffith is a farmer.
Kradu Grimblade is a weaponsmith trainer. He says the best defense is a good offense.
Zula Slagfury is an armorsmith trainer. Her advice puts survival before weapon skill: a strong weapon is useless if its wielder does not live long enough to use it.
Montok Redhands is the Warsong Gulch battlemaster. He greets visitors in the Horde’s manner and speaks of the ongoing fight against the Silverwing Sentinels, welcoming their presence in the conflict.
Haelga Slatefist is the Alterac Valley battlemaster. Her greetings speak of returning from Outland to fight the Horde; she also warns an inexperienced visitor that the valley is dangerous.
Lylandor is the Warsong Gulch battlemaster. He points to the Silverwing Sentinels’ continuing fight against the Horde and asks whether the player will return to help them.

Adam Eternum is the Arathi Basin battlemaster, searching for powerful artifacts to aid the League of Arathor against the Defilers. He jokes that his Outland search has yielded a magical loincloth, a gnome sidekick, and an undead stalker accusing him of stealing a grey skull, then invites the player to join the League.

Keldor the Lost is the Arathi Basin battlemaster and seeks a way to defeat the League of Arathor. He complains that Adam Eternum hounds his every move, then appeals to returning slayers to help defeat the Alliance.
Wolf-Sister Maka is the Alterac Valley battlemaster. She reminds the player that battles still rage in Azeroth and asks them to return to help the Horde there.
A G'eras Vindicator in Shattrath City.
Oric Coe provides comic relief and should not be paid attention to, since doing so would only encourage him.
Iravar is an Eye of the Storm battlemaster.
Yula the Fair is an Eye of the Storm battlemaster.
Battle-Tiger is Adam Eternum's pet, a giant, armored, saddle-bearing attack cat.
Arodis Sunblade keeps Sha'tari artifacts and offers goods and repairs.
Asuur keeps Sha'tari artifacts and offers goods and repairs.
Iorioa is a portal trainer who says portal magic is something only a mage can learn.
Scribe Saalyn is an Aldor inscriptions scribe in Shattrath. She offers a vendor service, and her title distinguishes her from the Scryer scribe nearby.
Scribe Veredis is a Scryer inscriptions scribe in Shattrath. He offers a vendor service, and his title distinguishes him from the Aldor scribe nearby.
"Backstab" Bindo Gearbomb is an arena battlemaster for the Steamwheedle Fighting Circuit. His challenge is caustic: he dismisses unconvincing contenders and tells them to stop wasting his time.

Tobias the Filth Gorger is a Broken trader in Shattrath whose business connects bloodthistle with rotten arakkoa eggs. He is cagey when questioned about bloodthistle, but readily does business over an egg; his grotesque appetite and matter-of-fact return to business make him memorable.
Almaador is the Sha'tari quartermaster in Shattrath and offers a vendor service. His title marks the Sha'tari role he serves.
Gordie is a humanoid in Shattrath City.
Ilthuril is a stable master.
Oruhe is a stable master.
Nakodu serves as Lower City Quartermaster, with vendor access for browsing goods.
Veynna Dawnstar is a Keeper of Sha'tari Heirlooms, serving as a vendor.
Kelara is a Keeper of Sha'tari Heirlooms, serving as a vendor.
The widely placed Eye of the Storm Emissary serves a battleground role. Its menu offers a battleground travel option and describes Draenei forces and Alliance allies fighting the Horde in Outland.

An Eye of the Storm Envoy calls on allies to defend the battleground's mana cells from the draenei and can direct visitors into the fight. Envoys appear across several regions, carrying that appeal beyond the battlefield.

Nasmara Moonsong is a mooncloth specialist in Shattrath's Lower City. She offers to teach tailors the specialization, testing them with a sample of primal mooncloth made at Cenarion Refuge's moonwell. She examines the returned cloth and praises a fine sample, while her specialty also includes working with primal mooncloth.

Andrion Darkspinner is a shadoweave specialist in Shattrath's Lower City. He offers to teach the specialization, asking candidates to use a crystal at the Altar of Shadows in eastern Shadowmoon Valley to deepen their attunement. He recognizes a successful visit by a subtle change in the tailor, and offers help with shadoweave patterns and knowledge.

Gidge Spellweaver is Shattrath's resident spellfire tailoring expert. She researches nether-wraith essence, warns that spellfire tailoring is dangerous, and concluded that the wraiths and their environment are the same thing.
Sinnea Starsong is identified as a Lunar Festival herald.

Rilak the Redeemed is an arakkoa who says that, through A'dal, he learned of the Light and redemption after his people abused dark magic. He fears Terokk's return and points to Kirrik, who rejected Terokk's claim to prophecy and led others away from Skettis. Rilak distinguishes arakkoa changed by the naaru from those still living in the wild.
Redeemed Avian represents several avians rather than a single named individual.

Grashna is a defender in Shattrath’s fight against Skettis. Grashna rallies defenders against Terokk’s minions, calls them to arms when Terokk’s Avatar appears, and celebrates its defeat with a vow of death to Terokk and Skettis.
A beast called an Ambient Minion of Terokk in Shattrath City.

Vekax is an outcast in Shattrath who says Skettis loyalists mark the outcasts for death and that leaving the city walls is too dangerous. Vekax retaliates by seeking feathers from Terokkar’s Veils as proof of attacks on the enemy, offering treasure and expressing satisfaction in the outcasts’ resistance to Skettis.

Lonika Stillblade founded a rogue academy in Shattrath and teaches rogue tactics with a sardonic, irreverent style. Refugees and the naaru’s need for buildings have forced her to close the academy for now, but she intends to find a new site. She favors stealthy weapons, rejects maces, and warns rogues to prepare for mishaps when working with others.
V'eru's voice fills the listener's mind with crystalline clarity, then asks them to aid Grok, an ogre in Shattrath who is pleading for help.

Orphan Matron Mercy speaks with concern for children orphaned by Outland's conflicts and says they need hope for a bright future. She offers visitors options to replace Draenei or Blood Elf orphan whistles and warmly asks after their time with Dornaa or Salandria.

Grok is an ogre sent by Mog'dorg the Wizened to seek help for the Bloodmaul clan. He says the Bladespire clan has gronn allies and urges visitors to help in Blade's Edge. Frustrated when ignored, he threatens to smash the unhelpful; he also remarks that he is hungry and eyes some fruit.
Aldor Reveler is a Netherstorm world-event celebrant who performs random emotes while out of combat.
Eebee Jinglepocket is a Smokywood Pastures vendor who offers goods in Netherstorm.
Olnayvi Copperpinch is a Smokywood Pastures vendor who also handles quest inquiries.
Peacekeeper Jadaar is a humanoid peacekeeper in Shattrath City.
Brendan Turner is a meat vendor who sells provisions in Shattrath City.
Vindicator Aeus asks visitors to assist Exarch Orelis, whose group is investigating the activities of Kael'thas and his minions in Netherstorm.

Vindicator Kaan is a named vindicator stationed in Netherstorm. Kaan directs a request for support to Exarch Orelis, whose small team was sent to investigate Kael’thas and his forces. The appeal reflects concern that the local presence may be too weak for the work ahead.

Arcanist Savan is a named arcanist in Netherstorm who sends reinforcements toward Spymaster Thalodien. The dispatch follows a report that Thalodien has encountered something important while investigating Kael’thas; Savan asks the traveler to report to him and help as needed.

Arcanist Raestan is a named arcanist in Netherstorm associated with the request to reinforce Spymaster Thalodien. Thalodien’s team was investigating Kael’thas, and his brief report pointed to something important; the traveler is sent to report to him and assist.

Barthamus is a creature in Shattrath’s Lower City who calls himself the abandoned child of a monster. After the adventurer’s campaign against the Dragonmaw, he speaks with deep gratitude and says his kin have offered to join the mission in Outland. He treats the meeting as the close of a long adventure.

Yuula, Shattrath’s Recruitment Officer, recruits for the Skyguard, sworn to protect the city from threats above. Yuula tests whether a prospective recruit can fight as well as fly, and sends them against nearby Gordunni ogres. Yuula also directs new recruits to Sergeant Doryn as the Skyguard confronts rising arakkoa activity near Skettis.

Suraku is an Azure Netherwing drake who expresses honor at meeting the adventurer and gratitude for their aid to the Netherwing Dragonflight. Suraku says the flight has watched the adventurer’s exploits and offers, if chosen as a companion, to carry them across the world and help as requested.

Jorus is a cobalt Netherwing drake who expresses gratitude for aid to the dragonflight and offers companionship on journeys in Outland. If chosen, Jorus promises to fly far with the traveler and do his best to honor their requests.
Onyxien is the Onyx Netherwing Drake, a potential travel companion who offers to fly the traveler around Outland if selected.

Malfas is a purple Netherwing drake who expresses gratitude for aid to the dragonflight and offers companionship on journeys in Outland. If chosen, Malfas promises to fly far with the traveler and try to honor their requests.

Zoya is a veridian Netherwing drake who expresses gratitude for aid to the dragonflight and offers companionship on journeys in Outland. If chosen, Zoya promises to fly far with the traveler and try to honor their requests.

Voranaku is a violet Netherwing drake who expresses gratitude for aid to the dragonflight and offers companionship on journeys in Outland. If chosen, Voranaku promises to fly far with the traveler and try to honor their requests.

Arcanist Xorith is a Scryer apothecary dealing in alchemical goods. Xorith regards experience fighting Illidan's powerful minions, and esteem among the Sha'tar, Cenarion Expedition and Scryers, as signs of a customer's worthiness.

Haldor the Compulsive is an Aldor apothecary who speaks of his alchemical goods as rewards for bringing marks from Illidan’s most powerful minions. He also describes a higher threshold tied to exalted standing with the Sha'tar, Cenarion Expedition, and Aldor, making his service deliberately selective.

Kevin Browning styles himself a coffee aficionado. His menu pairs a coffee request with an impatient, dismissive rebuke: he says he has places to go and people to see, then calls the listener a peasant. His manner is brusque and hurried.
Investigator Asric is a humanoid investigator in Shattrath City.

Apprentice Tasserel says a mentor sent him to seek assistance in Lower City. He feels confined there, describing limits on leaving and unhelpful patrons, but sees an adventurous listener as a possible ally. He directs that listener to Archmage Alturus near Karazhan and says he plans to seek access to more of the city; he also mentions an old associate rumored to be there.

Wind Trader Zhareem brokers rare and precious objects for clients with tastes ranging from the mundane to the exotic. He treats unusual requests as business, offers a commission, and values his reputation enough to honor a client's purchase even when tempted to keep an item for himself. His remarks show curiosity about what he trades, though he admits he may not understand the consequences of time travel.

Nether-Stalker Mah'duun works in Lower City, where he directs bounty hunters against threats named by the nether winds. He says he hears their orders, speaks of himself by name, and does not know when the next command will come; he expects the winds to whisper again the following day.

The Rokk is a master cook in Lower City who develops unusual dishes, from spirit-soaked soup to food broiled over an abyssal's remains. He admits he has lost his own sense of adventure, but recognizes it in younger cooks and invites them to help with his recipes. He prizes rare ingredients and praises cooks who bring him good results.
An image bearing the name Vazruden the Herald.
Grisy Spicecrackle is identified as a kitchen assistant in the Netherstorm area.
Gargoth is identified as a kitchen assistant in the Netherstorm area.
The Consortium Assistant is a Consortium-associated figure found in Netherstorm.
Known as the Thunderbrew “Apprentice,” this vendor offers Thunderbrew goods.
Caylee Dak is an Aldor-associated Shattrath resident, as described by Alicia, who calls Caylee her friend and sends her a poem. Caylee’s recorded greeting invokes the Light of Elune.
Dusky is identified as Caylee’s pet in Shattrath.

Exarch Nasuun leads the Shattered Sun Offensive’s effort to build a magical portal from Shattrath to the Isle of Quel’Danas and the Sunwell. He explains that the portal needs a powerful energy source and continued mana-cell supplies to stay open.

Lord Torvos supports the offensive on Quel’Danas from Shattrath. He fears Kael’thas’s Sunfury counterattack in Outland will divert troops from the Sunwell and seeks their attack plans from Netherstorm. He values every fighter on the front lines and urges vigilance even after the plans are recovered.
Commander Steele is stationed in Shattrath.

General Tiras'alan is a military figure on the Isle of Quel'Danas during the crisis at the Sunwell. He warns that Kil'jaeden's rise through the Sunwell would bring a vast war.
Marksman Bova provides specialty ammunition and repair services on the Isle of Quel'Danas.
Archer Delvinar provides specialty ammunition and repair services on the Isle of Quel'Danas.

Whirligig Wafflefry is a Gnomish inventor on the Isle of Quel'Danas who pitches an Ultra-Kinetic Waffle Iron and an Electrostatic Maculation Blaster. Wafflefry says the stain-blasting device derives from Shattered Sun Offensive military technology, and urges a harbinger to return with research results by dangling the waffle iron as a reward.

Fire Eater is a Master Fire Eater associated with the Fire Festival and appears across many regions. Festival greetings invite visitors to enjoy the celebration and honor its flame, while other lines warn them to avoid burns. The associated Playing with Fire quest describes fire tricks as skills to learn and directs Alliance players to a Master Fire Eater.

Zephyr is a dragonkin who offers passage to the Caverns of Time. In conversation, Zephyr reflects that the world has been damaged beyond what can be seen and that even the passage of time feels different.

Kixi the Shiv is an Arena Battlemaster associated with the Steamwheedle Fighting Circuit. Kixi bluntly challenges would-be fighters, dismissing one character's prospects and asking another whether they think they can compete.
A Big Bruiser, a humanoid in Shattrath City.

Flame Eater is a Master Flame Eater associated with the Fire Festival and appears across many regions. Festival greetings invite visitors to enjoy the celebration and honor its flame, while other lines warn them to avoid burns. The associated Playing with Fire quest describes fire tricks as skills to learn and directs Horde players to a Master Flame Eater.
